method: After freezing and replaying the record, reread the 2026–27 faculty regulations and errata and the current student curriculum. Reconstructed the 75 plus 45 plus 15 plus 45 EC structure, checked compulsory and recommended courses, level rules and the three research prerequisites. Reconsidered the finished options from actual UCR psychology, computation, communication and organization course evidence and rechecked the remaining educational specialization gaps. This is a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The 2026–27 faculty regulations and current student curriculum establish 180 EC: 135 major and 45 profiling. Ten compulsory taught courses account for 75 EC; six 7.5 EC major electives and the required 15 EC thesis complete the major. The student model places two recommended major electives and one open major choice in year one, three major choices in year two and 45 EC of profiling in year three. The older comparison incorrectly treated the action research lab, internship and selected multilingual course as a fixed example and inserted generic reconciliation credits. These courses are optional under the current rules. Tutorial and portfolio requirements carry zero EC. The full-time bachelor is mainly Dutch, with individual courses offered in English. The teaching qualification variant is a distinct structured variant and is outside this generic comparison.

The level rules require at least 45 EC advanced overall, at least 37.5 EC each advanced and intermediate in the major subject to the advanced-credit substitution rule, and at least 15 EC intermediate or advanced in profiling. The four compulsory advanced courses and thesis provide 45 advanced EC. Four required intermediate courses and the recommended Organization Studies course provide 37.5 intermediate EC. Context courses marked in the annex provide at least 15 EC. The thesis requires passing introductory and applied research methods and Methods in Educational Research. An internship, if selected, requires 120 bachelor EC. The student model places the thesis over blocks 3–4 in year three. Choices are left within the approved lists and level rules.

The broad plan connects development, social psychology and evidence synthesis with social inequality, legal and policy structures and quantitative and qualitative inquiry. Public Policy Analysis adds explicit policy reasoning and memo writing. The cognition plan uses neurobiology, language acquisition, attention, memory and development to frame learning, while programming, statistics, machine learning and ethics provide general tools for investigating behavior and technology. Community rhetoric adds communication practice and youth resilience adds school climate and belonging. These skills do not reproduce instructional design or specialist digital pedagogy. The organizational plan replaces generic advanced algorithms and neural models with leadership communication, negotiation, decision-making and policy analysis while retaining organizational psychology, digital strategy, data and research. The three plans differ in advanced core and organizing focus. Developmental psychology and general research courses provide bounded overlap, while education-specific design, evaluation instruments, action research and specialist thesis remain distinct. UCR optional independent research sits outside the 180 EC degree.
